# `pygeovision infer`

Tiled inference on a GeoTIFF (or a folder of them) with **your trained model**: the image is cut into overlapping chips,
each is predicted, and the results are blended into one seamless raster. See [Inference](../../inference/index.md).

## When to use it

Use it after training, to map a scene larger than GPU memory.

## What you get

A class-map GeoTIFF on the input grid (`uint8`, 255 = nodata) and a summary of chips and time.

## Things to know

* `--checkpoint` is required and loaded strictly; no other model is ever substituted.
* `--normalise` (the default) stretches each band to its 2–98 percentile range. If you trained on reflectance 0–1 pass
  `--no-normalise`, or the model sees differently scaled data ([why it matters](../../inference/index.md#matching-the-input-to-training)).
* `--classes` and `--in-channels` must match the checkpoint.

## Commands

```text
Usage: pygeovision infer [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Run AI inference on satellite imagery.

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  batch    Run batch inference on a directory of GeoTIFFs with your trained model.
  predict  Run tiled inference on a GeoTIFF with your trained model.
```

### `pygeovision infer batch`

```text
Usage: pygeovision infer batch [OPTIONS] INPUT_DIR OUTPUT_DIR

  Run batch inference on a directory of GeoTIFFs with your trained model.

Options:
  -m, --model TEXT              Registry model name.  [default: unet_resnet50]
  --checkpoint PATH             Your trained weights for --model (state dict from GeoTrainer).
                                [required]
  -c, --classes INTEGER         [default: 2]
  --in-channels INTEGER         Bands the model was trained on (default: the first input
                                file's).
  -w, --workers INTEGER         [default: 2]
  --pattern TEXT                [default: *.tif]
  --overwrite                   Predict again even if the output file already exists (default:
                                skip those files).
  --normalise / --no-normalise  Stretch every band to its own 2-98 percentile range before the
                                model sees it. Use --no-normalise if the model was trained on
                                values that were already scaled (for example reflectance 0-1),
                                otherwise the prediction is made on differently scaled data and
                                can be wrong.  [default: normalise]
  --help                        Show this message and exit.
```

### `pygeovision infer predict`

```text
Usage: pygeovision infer predict [OPTIONS] IMAGE_PATH

  Run tiled inference on a GeoTIFF with your trained model.

Options:
  -m, --model TEXT                Registry model name.  [default: unet_resnet50]
  --checkpoint PATH               Your trained weights for --model (state dict from GeoTrainer).
                                  [required]
  -o, --output TEXT
  -c, --classes INTEGER           [default: 2]
  --in-channels INTEGER           Bands the model was trained on (default: the input's).
  --chip-size INTEGER             [default: 512]
  --overlap INTEGER               [default: 64]
  --blend [gaussian|linear|constant]
                                  [default: gaussian]
  --device TEXT                   cuda|cpu|mps
  --normalise / --no-normalise    Stretch every band to its own 2-98 percentile range before the
                                  model sees it. Use --no-normalise if the model was trained on
                                  values that were already scaled (for example reflectance 0-1),
                                  otherwise the prediction is made on differently scaled data
                                  and can be wrong.  [default: normalise]
  --help                          Show this message and exit.
```
